meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes, so let's start with why my son has a zero.
I didn't come for thanks. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, Hale. I've done this for twenty years. Answer my question: who decided, and when?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
I'm not discussing Owen's October with you, Hale. You've asked me three questions and answered none of mine: who decided, and was he heard before it went in the gradebook?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I don't answer "possible" about my son. Either you have a document with a date on it, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.
I said nothing of the kind, and I'm writing down that you put those words in my mouth. Show me what you have, Hale, or tell me you have nothing.
